stem:
Sameer compares $p^{2}+q^{2}=r^{2}$ with $p^{n}+q^{n}=r^{n}$ for integers $n>2$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Both equations are Baudhāyana triples under one shared name.
Positive natural-number solutions exist for the square case, but Fermat's claim says none when $n>2$.
The equations match because both print a plus sign between powers.
Applying $a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$ to a right triangle also settles $p^{n}+q^{n}=r^{n}$ for $n>2$.

teacher.key_rationale: Baudhāyana triples solve the square-power equation. Fermat's Last Theorem denies positive natural-number solutions for n>2. Shared plus signs or right-triangle reasoning do not settle the higher-power case.
